title: ~지 않다 [ji anta] (Negative form)
shortExplanation: Used to negate verbs/adjectives; equivalent to 'not' in English.
longExplanation: '~지 않다 [ji anta]' creates the negative form of verbs or adjectives, similar to 'not' in English. It indicates that an action does not happen or a state does not exist.

examples.sentence: 저는 매일 아침밥을 먹지 않아요. 대신에 과일을 먹어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun maeil achimbabeul meokji anhayo. Daesine gwail-eul meogeoyo.
examples.translation: I don't eat breakfast every morning. Instead, I eat fruit.

examples.sentence: 우리 할머니는 한국에 살지 않아요, 미국에 살아요.
examples.romanization: Uri halmeonineun hanguge salji anhayo, miguge sarayo.
examples.translation: Our grandmother doesn't live in Korea, she lives in America.

examples.sentence: 나는 이런 상황을 좋아하지 않아요. 나에게 스트레스를 줘요.
examples.romanization: Naneun ireon sanghwangeul johahaji anhayo. Na-ege seuteureseureul jwoyo.
examples.translation: I do not like these kinds of situations; they give me stress.

examples.sentence: 당신은 그 사람을 알지 않아요? 그는 우리 학교에서 유명한 선생님이에요.
examples.romanization: Dangsineun geu sarameul alji anhayo? Geuneun uri hakgyoeseo yumyeonghan seonsaengnimieyo.
examples.translation: Don't you know that person? He is a famous teacher at our school.

title: ~지 않아도 되다 [ji anado dweda] (Don't have to)
shortExplanation: Used to express that an action is not necessary or mandatory; 'don't have to'.
longExplanation: '~지 않아도 되다 [ji anado dweda]' indicates that someone is not obliged to perform a certain action. It literally means 'it is okay even if you do not do something.'

examples.sentence: 너무 걱정하지 않아도 돼. 모두 잘 될 거야.
examples.romanization: Neomu geokjeonghaji anado dwae. Modu jal doel geoya.
examples.translation: You don't have to worry too much. Everything will be fine.

examples.sentence: 시험을 이미 통과했기 때문에 더 이상 공부하지 않아도 돼.
examples.romanization: Siheomeul imi tonggwahaetgi ttaemune deo isang gongbuhaji anado dwae.
examples.translation: You don't need to study anymore because you've already passed the exam.

examples.sentence: 우리는 다른 사람들을 위해 모든 것을 포기하지 않아도 돼.
examples.romanization: Urineun dareun saramdeureul wihae modeun geoseul pogihaji anado dwae.
examples.translation: We don't have to give up everything for other people.

examples.sentence: 비가 온다고 해서 그냥 집에 머무르지 않아도 돼.
examples.romanization: Biga ondago haeseo geunyang jibe meomureuji anado dwae.
examples.translation: You don’t have to stay home just because it's raining.

title: 지만 [jiman] (but)
shortExplanation: Used to express contrast between two statements, similar to 'but' in English.
longExplanation: '지만 [jiman]' is a common conjunction in Korean that expresses contrast or contradiction between two clauses, much like 'but' in English. The second clause contradicts or provides an unexpected twist to the first clause.

examples.sentence: 오늘은 일찍 일어났지만, 학교에 늦었어요. 버스를 놓쳐서 그래요.
examples.romanization: Oneureun iljjik ireonatjiman, hakgyoe neujeosseoyo. Beoseureul nochyeoseo geuraeyo.
examples.translation: I woke up early today, but I was late for school because I missed the bus.

examples.sentence: 공부를 많이 하지만, 아직 이해가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.romanization: Gongbureul mani hajiman, ajik ihaega jal an dwaeyo.
examples.translation: I study a lot, but I still don't understand it well.

examples.sentence: 철수는 키가 작지만 매우 강력한 사람이에요.
examples.romanization: Cheolsuneun kiga jakjiman maeu gangnyeokhan saramieyo.
examples.translation: Chulsoo is short, but he's very strong.

examples.sentence: 여기 음식은 맛있지만 가격이 너무 비싸요.
examples.romanization: Yeogi eumsik-eun masitjiman gagyeogi neomu bissayo.
examples.translation: The food here is delicious, but it's too expensive.

title: ~지요 [jiyo] (Isn't it? Right?)
shortExplanation: Used to confirm or check agreement with the listener, akin to a polite tag question.
longExplanation: '~지요 [jiyo]' is a sentence ending used in Korean to ask for confirmation or acknowledgment from the listener. It's often used in polite or friendly conversation to invite agreement or verify shared knowledge, similar to saying 'isn't it?' or 'right?' in English.

examples.sentence: 날씨가 많이 추워졌지요? 스카프를 챙기는 게 좋겠어요.
examples.romanization: Nalssiga mani chuwajyeotjiyo? Seukapeureul chaenggineun ge jokesseoyo.
examples.translation: It's gotten quite cold, hasn't it? We should bring a scarf.

examples.sentence: 우리 다음 주에 시험 있지요? 공부 시작해야겠어요.
examples.romanization: Uri daeum jue siheom itjiyo? Gongbu sijakhaeyagesseoyo.
examples.translation: We have an exam next week, right? We should start studying.

examples.sentence: 이번 주말에 친구들과 캠핑 가기로 했지요? 준비가 좀 더 필요할 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Ibeon jumale chingudeulgwa kaemping gagiro haetjiyo? Junbiga jom deo pilyohal geot gatayo.
examples.translation: We decided to go camping with friends this weekend, didn't we? I think we need more preparation.

examples.sentence: 요즘 일이 많아서 힘들지요? 휴식이 정말 필요한 때 같아요.
examples.romanization: Yojeum iri manhaseo himdeuljiyo? Hyusigi jeongmal pilyohan ttae gatayo.
examples.translation: Work's been tough lately, hasn't it? It seems like we really need a break.

title: ~진 않지만 [jin anhjiman] (Not exactly, but)
shortExplanation: Used to express that something is not entirely true but partially or somewhat so.
longExplanation: '~진 않지만 [jin anhjiman]' indicates that a certain condition is not exactly or fully met, yet there is some partial truth or a mitigating factor. It softens the statement, showing modesty or a lesser degree than expected.

examples.sentence: 네가 좋아하는 그 영화, 난 별로 재미있진 않지만 볼 만했어.
examples.romanization: Nega joahaneun geu yeonghwa, nan byeollo jaemiitjin anhjiman bol manhaesseo.
examples.translation: That movie you like wasn't exactly fun for me, but it was worth watching.

examples.sentence: 그가 말한 건 중요하진 않지만, 알아 두면 좋을 거야.
examples.romanization: Geuga malhan geon jungyohajin anhjiman, ara dumyeon jo-eul geoya.
examples.translation: What he said isn't exactly important, but it's good to keep in mind.

examples.sentence: 네가 준 선글라스, 예쁘진 않지만 꽤 유용해.
examples.romanization: Nega jun seongleoseu, yeppeujin anhjiman kkwae yuyonghae.
examples.translation: The sunglasses you gave me aren't exactly pretty, but they're quite useful.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 아주 유명하진 않지만 충분히 재능이 있어.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun aju yumyeonghajin anhjiman chungbunhi jaeneung-i isseo.
examples.translation: She's not very famous, but she definitely has talent.

title: ~쯤 [jjeum] (About, around)
shortExplanation: A postposition indicating approximation or estimation (time, quantity, degree).
longExplanation: '~쯤 [jjeum]' is used in Korean to show a rough estimate or approximation, similar to 'about,' 'around,' or 'approximately' in English. It's often used in casual conversation to give an inexact notion of time, number, or degree.

examples.sentence: 회사에는 오후 3시쯤 도착할 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Hoesa-eneun ohu sam si jjeum dochakhal geot gatayo.
examples.translation: I think I'll arrive at the office around 3 PM.

examples.sentence: 어제 그녀는 약 열 개쯤 쿠키를 먹었어요.
examples.romanization: Eoje geunyeoneun yak yeol gae jjeum kukireul meogeosseoyo.
examples.translation: She ate about ten cookies yesterday.

examples.sentence: 여기서 학교까지 걸어서 15분쯤 걸릴 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Yeogiseo hakgyokkaji georeoseo sip-o bun jjeum geolril geot gatayo.
examples.translation: It will take about 15 minutes to walk from here to the school.

examples.sentence: 그는 이미 오백 페이지쯤 읽어서 곧 책을 다 읽을 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun imi obaek peiji jjeum ilgeoseo got chaegeul da ilgeul geot gatayo.
examples.translation: He's already read about five hundred pages, so he'll likely finish the book soon.

title: ~처럼 [cheoreom] (Like, as)
shortExplanation: Used to compare two things or indicate that something behaves similarly to something else.
longExplanation: '처럼 [cheoreom]' is a postposition in Korean that draws a comparison between two things, states, or actions, similar to 'like' or 'as' in English. It indicates that one entity resembles another in appearance, manner, or feeling.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 천사처럼 생겼어요. 얼굴이 매우 예쁘고 순수해 보여요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun cheonsacheoreom saenggyeosseoyo. Eolguli maeu yeppeugo sunsuhae boyeoyo.
examples.translation: She looks like an angel. Her face is very pretty and she looks pure.

examples.sentence: 이 음식은 어머니가 만든 것처럼 맛있어요. 집밥 느낌이 나요.
examples.romanization: I eumsigeun eomeoniga mandeun geotcheoreom masisseoyo. Jibbab neukkimi nayo.
examples.translation: This food tastes like something my mother would cook. It feels like homemade food.

examples.sentence: 그는 꿈에서 본 사람처럼 보여서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun kkumeseo bon saramcheoreom boyeoseo kkamjjak nollaesseoyo.
examples.translation: He looked like the person I saw in my dream, and it surprised me.

examples.sentence: 태양이 뜨면 마치 새로운 세상이 열린 것처럼 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.romanization: Taeyangi tteumyeon machi saeroun sesangi yeollin geotcheoreom gibuni joajyeoyo.
examples.translation: When the sun rises, I feel as if a new world has opened.

title: ~층 [cheung] (Floor count)
shortExplanation: Used to express the number of floors in a building, like 'nth floor'.
longExplanation: '~층 [cheung]' is a suffix in Korean denoting which floor of a building is being referred to. It attaches to a numeral to indicate the ordinal floor number, similar to English expressions like 'the 3rd floor', 'the 15th floor', etc.

examples.sentence: 저희 집은 아파트 건물의 15층에 위치하고 있습니다.
examples.romanization: Jeohui jip-eun apateu geonmul-ui sib-o cheung-e wichihago itsseumnida.
examples.translation: Our home is located on the 15th floor of the apartment building.

examples.sentence: 회사는 높은 건물의 20층에 있어서 전망이 정말 좋습니다.
examples.romanization: Hoesa-neun nopeun geonmul-ui isip cheung-e isseoseo jeonmangi jeongmal joseumnida.
examples.translation: The company is on the 20th floor of a tall building, so the view is really good.

examples.sentence: 엘리베이터가 없으면 10층까지 걸어서 올라가야 합니다.
examples.romanization: Ellibeiteoga eobseumyeon sip cheung-kkaji georeoseo ollagaya hamnida.
examples.translation: If there is no elevator, you have to walk up to the 10th floor.

examples.sentence: 복층 아파트 구조는 일반적으로 2층 건물로 설계됩니다.
examples.romanization: Bokcheung apateu gujoneun ilbanjeogeuro i-cheung geonmul-lo seolgyedoemnida.
examples.translation: A duplex apartment structure is typically designed as a two-story building.

title: ~(으)ㄹ지 (Maybe, perhaps)
shortExplanation: Used to express uncertainty, doubt, or speculation; 'might', 'maybe', 'I'm not sure if...'.
longExplanation: The grammar pattern '~(으)ㄹ지' is used with verbs or adjectives to convey uncertainty or speculation. It often appears with expressions like '모르겠다 (I don't know)', forming '~(으)ㄹ지 모르겠다' to mean 'I’m not sure if...' or 'maybe...'. It's similar to 'perhaps' or 'might' in English.

examples.sentence: 오늘은 비가 올지 모르겠어요, 아침에는 맑았거든요.
examples.romanization: Oneureun biga olji moreugesseoyo, achim-eneun malgatgeodeunyo.
examples.translation: I’m not sure if it will rain today; it was clear in the morning.

examples.sentence: 그 학생이 시험을 통과할지 잘 모르겠어요. 공부를 열심히 안 해서요.
examples.romanization: Geu haksaengi siheomeul tonggwahalji jal moreugesseoyo. Gongbureul yeolsimhi an haeseo-yo.
examples.translation: I'm not sure if that student will pass the exam, because he didn't study hard.

examples.sentence: 그녀가 이렇게 많이 먹을 수 있을지 몰랐어요. 항상 조금만 먹었거든요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoga ireohge manhi meogeul su isseulji mollasseoyo. Hangsang jogeumman meogeotgeodeunyo.
examples.translation: I didn’t know she could eat this much; she usually only ate small amounts.

examples.sentence: 저를 사랑하실지 아직 잘 모르겠어요. 그분의 마음을 아직 잘 몰라요.
examples.romanization: Jeoreul saranghasilji ajik jal moreugesseoyo. Geubunui maeumeul ajik jal mollayo.
examples.translation: I’m still not sure if she loves me; I don’t know her feelings well yet.

title: ~마다 [mada] (Every, each)
shortExplanation: Used to express routines or regular occurrences; 'every', 'each'.
longExplanation: '~마다 [mada]' is a suffix in Korean used after time words or intervals to indicate repetition or regularity, similar to 'every' in English. For example, 매주 토요일마다 (every Saturday), 매일 아침마다 (every morning), 매월 마지막 주마다 (every last week of the month), etc.

examples.sentence: 나는 매주 토요일마다 운동을 합니다. 이렇게 규칙적으로 운동하면 건강에 좋아요.
examples.romanization: Naneun maeju toyoil-mada undongeul hamnida. Ireohge gyuchikjeogeuro undonghamyeon geongange joayo.
examples.translation: I exercise every Saturday. Exercising regularly like this is good for my health.

examples.sentence: 그는 일주일에 두 번씩 한국어를 공부해요, 그래서 한국어 실력이 빨리 향상되고 있어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun iljuire du beon-ssik hangugeoreul gongbuhaeyo, geuraeseo hangugeo silryeogi ppalli hyangsangdoego isseoyo.
examples.translation: He studies Korean twice a week, so his Korean skills are improving quickly.

examples.sentence: 우리는 매일 아침마다 만나서 함께 식사를 해요. 이게 우리의 일상적인 습관이에요.
examples.romanization: Urineun maeil achim-mada mannaseo hamkke siksareul haeyo. Ige uriui ilsangjeogin seupgwanieyo.
examples.translation: We meet every morning and have a meal together. That's our daily routine.

examples.sentence: 그녀는 매달 마지막 주 일요일마다 가족들과 모여요. 그렇게 시간을 보내는 게 그녀의 방식이에요.
examples.romanization: Geunyeoneun maedal majimak ju ilyoil-mada gajokdeulgwa moyeoyo. Geureohge siganeul bonaeneun ge geunyeoui bangsikieyo.
examples.translation: She gathers with her family on the last Sunday of each month. That's how she spends time with them.

title: ~(으)ㄹ 테니까 [tenikka] (So, therefore)
shortExplanation: Indicates an assumption or reason, leading to a suggestion or conclusion; 'because it will be...', 'so'.
longExplanation: '~(으)ㄹ 테니까' expresses the speaker’s assumption or strong guess about a future or present state, providing a reason for the following statement. For example, '배가 고플 테니까 (you must be hungry), so let's eat.' This form combines the future/assumed ending '~(으)ㄹ 테다' with '~니까 (because)'.

examples.sentence: 너무 배가 고플 테니까 빨리 식당에 가서 뭔가 먹어야겠어요.
examples.romanization: Neomu baega gopeul tenikka ppalli sikdang-e gaseo mwonga meogeoyagesseoyo.
examples.translation: You must be really hungry, so let's go to the restaurant quickly and get something to eat.

examples.sentence: 시험을 잘 보려면 많이 공부했을 테니까 꼭 좋은 점수를 받을 거예요.
examples.romanization: Siheomeul jal boryeomyeon manhi gongbuhaesseul tenikka kkok joeun jeomsureul badeul geoyeyo.
examples.translation: Since you probably studied a lot to do well on the test, I'm sure you'll get a good score.

examples.sentence: 우리는 곧 이 문제를 해결할 테니까 조금만 기다려 주세요.
examples.romanization: Urineun got i munjereul haegyeolhal tenikka jogeumman gidaryeo juseyo.
examples.translation: We will solve this problem soon, so please wait just a bit.

examples.sentence: 내가 금방 갈 테니까 먼저 준비하고 있어.
examples.romanization: Naega geumbang gal tenikka meonjeo junbihago isseo.
examples.translation: I’ll be there soon, so get things ready first.

title: ~편이다 [pyeonida] (It is preferable)
shortExplanation: Indicates a personal leaning, tendency, or preference; 'tend to', 'find it better to'.
longExplanation: The construction '~편이다 [pyeonida]' expresses that something is on the side of or tends to be a certain way. It conveys a personal preference or leaning. For example, '저는 집에서 공부하는 편이에요' means 'I tend to study at home' or 'I prefer studying at home.'
formation: Verb stem + (으)ㄴ/는 편이다 or Adjective + 편이다

examples.sentence: 저는 여름보다 겨울이 훨씬 즐거운 편이에요. 눈이 많이 오는 걸 좋아하거든요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun yeoreumboda gyeouli hwolssin jeulgeoun pyeonieyo. Nuni manhi oneun geol joahageodeunyo.
examples.translation: I find winter much more enjoyable than summer. I love it when it snows a lot.

examples.sentence: 사람들과 대화하는 게 은근히 어려운 편이라서, 보통은 메시지로 먼저 연락해요.
examples.romanization: Saramdeulgwa daehwahaneun ge eungeunhi eoryeoun pyeoniraseo, botongeun mesijiro meonjeo yeollakhaeyo.
examples.translation: I find talking to people somewhat difficult, so I usually contact them via messages first.

examples.sentence: 어렸을 때부터 수학 문제를 푸는 편이었어요. 그래서 나중에 수학 선생님이 되고 싶었죠.
examples.romanization: Eoryeosseul ttaebuteo suhak munjereul puneun pyeonieosseoyo. Geuraeseo najunge suhak seonsaengnimi doego sipeotjyo.
examples.translation: I've tended to be good at solving math problems since I was young, so I wanted to become a math teacher later on.

examples.sentence: 매운 음식을 좋아하는 편이라서, 자주 매운 라면을 먹습니다.
examples.romanization: Maewun eumsigeul joahaneun pyeoniraseo, jaju maewun ramyeoneul meokseumnida.
examples.translation: I generally prefer spicy food, so I often eat spicy ramen.

title: ~하다가 [hadaga] (Was doing something and then...)
shortExplanation: Indicates an ongoing action that is interrupted by another event; 'was doing... then...'.
longExplanation: '~하다가 [hadaga]' shows that one action was in progress when something else happened or changed. It often implies an unexpected interruption or switch of focus while the first activity was still ongoing.

examples.sentence: 저는 숙제를 하다가 친구가 전화해서 놀러 가자고 했어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun sukjereul hadaga chinguga jeonhwahaeseo nolleo gajago haesseoyo.
examples.translation: I was doing my homework when my friend called and suggested we go out.

examples.sentence: 저는 새벽에 산책을 하다가 갑자기 비가 왔어요.
examples.romanization: Jeoneun saebyeoke sanchaekeul hadaga gabjagi biga wasseoyo.
examples.translation: I was taking a walk at dawn when it suddenly started to rain.

examples.sentence: 어제 저는 밖에서 책을 읽다가 갑자기 배가 고파졌어요.
examples.romanization: Eoje jeoneun bakeseo chaekeul ilgdaga gabjagi baega gopajyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: Yesterday, I was reading a book outside when I suddenly became hungry.

examples.sentence: 나는 음악을 듣다가 어떤 노래가 내 기분에 맞아서 기분이 좋아졌어요.
examples.romanization: Naneun eumageul deudaga eotteon noraega nae gibune machaseo gibuni joajyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: I was listening to music, and then a certain song matched my mood, and I felt better.

title: ~하면 [hamyeon] (If, when)
shortExplanation: Expresses a condition or hypothetical situation; 'if', 'when'.
longExplanation: '~하면 [hamyeon]' introduces a conditional or hypothetical clause, much like 'if' or 'when' in English. It sets up a situation or requirement that triggers the outcome in the following clause.

examples.sentence: 나중에 시간이 더 많아지면, 더 많은 책을 읽을 수 있을 거예요.
examples.romanization: Najunge sigani deo manhajimyeon, deo manheun chaegeul ilgeul su isseul geoyeyo.
examples.translation: If I have more time later, I'll be able to read more books.

examples.sentence: 오늘 비가 오면, 우리는 영화를 보러 못 갈 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: Oneul biga omyeon, urineun yeonghwareul boreo mot gal geot gatayo.
examples.translation: If it rains today, we probably won't be able to go to the movies.

examples.sentence: 그가 우리에게 증거를 보여주면, 우리는 그를 믿을 거예요.
examples.romanization: Geuga urinege jeunggeoreul boyeojumyeon, urineun geureul mideul geoyeyo.
examples.translation: If he shows us the evidence, we'll believe him.

examples.sentence: 네가 학교를 더 열심히 다니면, 좋은 성적을 받을 수 있을 거야.
examples.romanization: Nega hakgyoreul deo yeolsimhi danimyeon, joeun seongjeogeul badeul su isseul geoya.
examples.translation: If you attend school more diligently, you'll be able to get good grades.

title: ~하면서 [hamyeonseo] (While doing)
longExplanation: '~하면서 [hamyeonseo]' is used to describe two actions happening at the same time or an action happening in the background while another action occurs. It's similar to 'while' or 'as' in English when describing simultaneous activities.

examples.sentence: 자연 속에서 힐링하면서 사진도 많이 찍었어요.
examples.romanization: Jayeon sogeseo hillinghamyeonseo sajindo mani jjigeosseoyo.
examples.translation: While healing in nature, I also took a lot of pictures.

examples.sentence: 음악을 들으면서 숙제를 했습니다.
examples.romanization: Eumageul deuleumyeonseo sukjereul haesseumnida.
examples.translation: I did my homework while listening to music.

examples.sentence: 아빠는 TV를 보면서 저녁을 드셨어요.
examples.romanization: Appaneun tibeireul bomyeonseo jeonyeogeul deusyeosseoyo.
examples.translation: Dad ate dinner while watching TV.

examples.sentence: 그는 걸으면서 책을 읽는 습관이 있어요.
examples.romanization: Geuneun georeumyeonseo chaekeul ilgneun seubgwani isseoyo.
examples.translation: He has a habit of reading books while walking.
